log-odds is the quantity ln(p/(1-p)); inverting it back to p is a move performed ON it, not something the definition depends on. The edge made a definition inherit 'expected: derivation' and fail its shape check forever.

retarget_edges.why: linearising a vector-valued f(x) is the first-order multivariate expansion; the Jacobian only appears in that form
the second-order test is stated on the Hessian, which the univariate expansion does not produce
the descent condition is a statement about the gradient inner product
an edge weight is defined on a weighted graph, which itself requires graph

marginalising a block Gaussian needs no integration and so no completing the square: the marginal is the affine image under a selection matrix A = [I 0], giving N(A mu, A Sigma A') = N(mu1, Sigma11). The old edge demanded a derivation no source performs -- Wikipedia states the result and says you simply drop the irrelevant variables -- so the check failed on every run.

seed_retargets.why: the EKF linearises a vector-valued process model; its Jacobian is a multivariate first-order term
the normal equations come from expanding a vector residual to first order
the descent argument is the multivariate first-order bound
quaternion renormalisation is division by the norm, not probability normalisation

add_edges.why: the EKF is the linear Kalman filter with F and H replaced by Jacobians, so the derivation it inherits -- the gain that minimises the posterior covariance -- lives there. Without this edge the EKF sheet correctly reports that its sources derive nothing, and the node that does carry the derivation is on no reader's path.
